docs.title: GTIA Dev Docs
docs.text:
Developer documentation for GregTech Infinity Ascension (GTIA), a GregTech modpack for Minecraft 1.20.1 built on GTCEu Modern, the GregTech Nexus Addon (GTNA) and GTIACore.

This site is for people who build the pack: what it is trying to be, how decisions are made, and how to write code for it. Players should start at the modpack repository.

Community: Discord · questions, bug reports and playtesting.

Section What you find there Vision The design pillars, what each tier is about, and the rules for each game system Governance Approved decisions and how releases work Development Building the mods, code conventions and GameTests

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text:
Repository Role GregTech-Infinity-Ascension The modpack: configs, KubeJS, quests, manifest GTIACore Core mod: pack machines, chemistry slices, GTIA Rules GregTech-Nexus-Addon GTNA: large machines, Nexus energy network, endgame multiblocks Agronomica Crop breeding mod (early development)

Policies that apply everywhere live in the organisation's .github repository: Code of Conduct, AI policy and contribution guidelines.

docs.title: Code conventions
docs.text: These rules apply to every mod in the organisation.

docs.title: Size
docs.text:
• Keep files small. A Java class over ~500 lines should be split by responsibility. A test class over ~800 lines should be split by system (multiblock/<machine>/, compat/<mod>/).
  • No giant log files. Do not keep growing ledgers, journals or "continuity" files in the repository. History belongs in git commits and changelogs; decisions belong in the decisions page.
  • One topic per pull request.

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
• Write comments only at key points: a non-obvious rule, a balance number with its reason, a workaround for another mod, a mixin target. Code that explains itself gets no comment.
  • No comments that repeat the code, no commented-out code, no "added by…", no TODOs without an issue.
  • Key comments are written in English, Portuguese and Chinese, so any developer can understand why the code is there:
// EN: Bees only open in GregTech machines; the Productive Bees centrifuge is removed.
// PT: O comb só abre em máquinas GT; a centrífuga do Productive Bees foi removida.
// ZH: 蜂巢只能在格雷科技机器中处理；已移除 Productive Bees 的离心机。

docs.title: Languages
docs.text:
• Every name a player can see ships in en_us, pt_br and zh_cn in the same commit. A GameTest fails when one is missing.
  • Commit messages, changelogs and public docs are in English.

docs.title: Content
docs.text:
• Content (machines, recipes, materials) lives in Java. KubeJS only removes or blocks recipes.
  • Multiblock tooltips follow the GTNA format (D-244).
  • The author's textures and art are never replaced without the author's approval.

docs.title: GameTests
docs.text:
Every mod runs its GameTests in CI with ./gradlew runGameTestServer. The rules below follow the Horizon-QA principles used by GTNH.

  1. Functional tests, not mocks. Place real blocks and run the real machine.
  2. Mock supply, not validation. A test may give a machine its inputs any way it likes, but it never bypasses recipe logic.
  3. Wait on state, not ticks. Tick counts are only timeouts.
  4. Negative tests matter. For every new multiblock, add at least a "forms" test and a test that it does not form, or does not run, when it should not.
  5. Leave no trace. Remove any block placed outside the template, and never leave a synthetic recipe registered.
  6. Failures explain themselves. The message says what went in, what was expected and what happened.

docs.title: Sweep tests
docs.text:
Each mod has tests that sweep over everything it registers, so new content is checked the day it is added:

  • every multiblock forms from its own preview;
  • no GT recipe has an empty input or output, or a duration of 0;
  • every machine tooltip builds without a raw translation key;
  • every name exists in en_us, pt_br and zh_cn.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: The pack targets under 4 GB of RAM on servers and clients, and Android through the Amethyst launcher. Every optimization goes in with numbers from before and after, measured the same way.

docs.title: How we measure
docs.text:
tools/perf_bench.py in the modpack boots a dedicated server with exactly the locked mods (median of 3 runs) and records:

Metric Meaning wall_s Seconds from launch until the server is ready done_s Minecraft's own "Done (…)" time (world preparation) heap_after_gc_mb Live heap after a forced full GC (class histogram) mspt Average server tick time while /gtialib bench keeps a grid of GT machines running

The client side uses tools/client_bench.py: it joins a test world on the Prism instance with a given heap limit and records live heap, RSS and out-of-memory errors.

python3 tools/perf_bench.py my-label --runs 3 --extra DIR_WITH_CANDIDATE_JARS \
    --tick gtceu:lv_electric_furnace:2000:minecraft:raw_iron --replace gtna=path/to/gtna.jar --off gtcovers

Results are appended to ~/MineProjects/GTIA-arquivo/perf/<label>.jsonl. Profiles use JFR (--jvm "-XX:StartFlightRecording=...").

docs.title: Results so far (GTIA, 129–134 mods, dedicated server)
docs.text: Change Where Before After Spawn chunks 441 → 25 (spawnchunks) Ascension Optimizer ready in 47 s, world prep 21.0 s, live heap 887 MB 31 s, 5.9 s, 625 MB Infinity cover check without building lists GTNA 8.37 ms/tick (2,000 working LV furnaces) 3.74 ms/tick Allocation-light getCovers() (gtcovers) Ascension Optimizer 8.37 ms/tick 3.93 ms/tick Multiblock EMI previews built on demand (gtpreviews) + soft shape cache in GTNA Ascension Optimizer, GTNA client in a world, 3 GB: live heap 1,947 MB, EMI reload 20.6 s; OOM at 1.5 GB 1,588 MB, 12.2 s; runs at 1.5 GB ModernFix dynamic_resources on, LeanObject server-only Pack config client live heap at the menu 1,030 MB (4 GB limit) 650 MB

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
1. Measure before writing the optimization; profile to find the real hotspot.
  2. Keep the optimization switchable (Ascension Optimizer features can be turned off in config/ascopt-mixins.properties).
  3. Run the mod's full GameTest suite after the change.
  4. Record the numbers in the commit, the changelog and this page.

docs.title: Tried and rejected
docs.text: Change Result Why it was dropped Cache RecipeHandlerList.doesCapabilityBypassDistinct() and skip the battery-slot copy in NotifiableEnergyContainer 4.29 → 4.51 ms/tick (runs vary 3.7–4.6 ms) No gain beyond noise; the remaining machine tick cost is spread over GTCEu's recipe handling ModernFix dynamic_resources with LeanObject on the client Client crash (ClassCastException in the model map) LeanObject's FastCollection replaces the map ModernFix expects; LeanObject became server-only Smaller GTCEu oreGenerationChunkCacheSize Not measured Can cut ore veins; only with proof that generation is identical

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
All mods target Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47.4.x, Java 17 and build with Gradle (ModDevGradle legacy Forge).

git clone https://github.com/GTInfinityAscension/GTIACore.git
cd GTIACore
./gradlew build
./gradlew runGameTestServer -PgtiaDevOptionalDependencies=true
Command What it does ./gradlew runClient Starts a development client ./gradlew runData Regenerates data (recipes, models, en_us.json) ./gradlew runGameTestServer Runs every GameTest headlessly and exits with an error on failure ./gradlew spotlessApply Formats the code

GTIACore needs GTNA and AE2 at runtime. Without them, pass -PgtiaDevOptionalDependencies=true so the test server can start.

docs.title: The modpack
docs.text: The pack is managed with packwiz. manifest/full.lock.json is the source of truth: tools/pack.py lock|fetch, then tools/packwiz_sync.py. Quests are generated from quests-src/ with tools/questgen.py build and checked with tools/questgen.py check.

docs.title: Organisation Maven
docs.text:
Released mod jars are published at https://gtinfinityascension.github.io/maven/ (no login needed). The maven repository checks for new GitHub releases every 6 hours and keeps the newest 5 versions of each artifact.

repositories {
    maven { url = 'https://gtinfinityascension.github.io/maven/' }
}
dependencies {
    modCompileOnly("com.raishxn.gtna:gtna:0.6.0") { transitive = false }
}

GTIACore compiles against GTNA from there. To compile against a local GTNA build instead, pass -PgtnaApiJar=/path/to/gtna.jar. To publish a new mod, add it to artifacts.json in the maven repository.

docs.title: Approved decisions
docs.text:
Product decisions have stable IDs (GTIA-D-NNN) that are never reused. Only the pack author approves a decision; a proposal is not a decision because it appears in a document. Revoked decisions keep their ID and are marked as revoked.

This page lists the approved product decisions that shape development. Internal drafts, audits and studies are not published.

ID Decision D-141 Greenhouse and Pyrolyse Oven arrive early in MV. The Greenhouse is optional and starts sun-dependent; the Pyrolyse Oven is strongly recommended but does not gate HV. D-221 Vertical, generated quest book (questgen.py) with chapters per tier, fixed meaning for side lanes and shapes per role, and automatic checks. D-226 No research tree. The pack is about building and running megafactories. D-227 Megafactory in depth and width. In the first 20 hours, new machines every session. 1–2 rebuilds per tier. The factory goes wherever the player wants. D-228 Processing lines grow with the tier (Steam 2–3, LV/MV 4–6, HV/EV 6–10, IV+ 10+), with by-products, closed loops, waste treatment and branching mid-line. D-229 Real chemistry without requiring a PhD, in the order Steam wood/coal and lime → LV chlor-alkali and steel → LV/MV Bayer + Hall-Héroult → MV Contact, Haber-Bosch + Ostwald, Solvay → HV refining. D-230 Resources: wells with purity, infinite sources per tier, planetary gases, renewables as real routes, mobs only from the Slaughterhouse, rare elements only as by-products. D-231 Energy: real fuel lines, heat as a resource, chemical and thermal storage, losses on wireless energy. D-232 Superseded by D-340. Logistics: no throughput limits, AE2 storage at the end of LV and autocrafting in MV, no Create. D-233 Multiblocks: upgrades by parts, Mega for everything, no limit, parallelism explained with numbers, modules through hatches and the GTNA module system, no luck-based progression. D-234 Danger: GTCEu explosions and hazards, cleanrooms, inert atmospheres, safety gear. D-237 Grind is solved with more factory. Own recipes for key items plus automatic shortcut checks. Modes chosen at world creation and locked. D-238 Chosen unique ideas: process conditions, two routes per molecule, closed loops, wells with purity, heat as a resource, factory dimension, planetary gases, rare elements only as by-products. D-244 Standard multiblock tooltips in the GTNA format: a real fact, then Main Function, Auxiliary Module and Running Requirements. D-246 Better versions of the real-chemistry multiblocks (rotary kiln, membrane cell…) come from IV/LuV onwards. D-254, D-256 GTIA Rules: Journey, Normal and Custom presets; 44 rules in 7 groups; rules never change registries. D-257 Crafting Chain (separate mod) replaces Fabricate. D-259 Bees arrive in HV through Productive Bees with its base recipes removed. D-260 Agronomica: our own crop mod, separate repository, LGPL-3.0. D-261 Ore boost with a reagent: 1 crushed + 1 leaf + reagent → 3 purified. D-262 GTIA Lib is the org's foundation library (depends on GTCEu); GTNA, GTIACore and Agronomica require it. GTOLib ideas are reimplemented from scratch, never copied. D-263 Ascension Optimizer (ascopt, no GT dependency): spawn chunks 441 → 25; server ready in 31 s instead of 47 s. D-264 Client uses ModernFix dynamic_resources; LeanObject is server-only (menu heap −37 %). D-265 EMI multiblock previews built on demand and GTNA shape cache in SoftReference: EMI reload 20.6 → 12.2 s, client runs with 1.5 GB. D-266 Draconium belongs to GTNA only; GTIACore's copy was removed. D-267 Agronomica core: crop sticks, four Steam/LV crops, Growth/Gain/Resistance (soft cap above 20), cross-breeding with mutations, NPK soil and fertilisers. D-268 HV bee line: all Productive Bees recipes and nests disabled; caged metal bees come from the Chemical Reactor, the Industrial Apiary (HV–UV) makes combs, combs give a small dust or, with HCl, purified ore. D-269 Recommended client flags: G1 periodic GC with free ratios 10–30 % and MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2; client RSS 6.0 → 4.4 GB with the same live heap. D-270 No batched @Synced for now: a player next to 500 working LV furnaces receives about 1.3 KB/s; LDLib sync is not a network bottleneck. D-275 HV quest chapter v6 approved: every dependency has a recipe reason checked against a GTNH 2.9 / GTO 0.6 quest atlas; tier machines are side quests unless a goal needs them; the circuit ladder (HV → EV → IV) lives inside the tier; the EV circuit comes right after the Cleanroom because HV multiblocks need it. D-276 Start–MV quest chapters v7 in game, built like HV v6: recipe reason on every dependency, tier motor and turbine as central hubs, LV motor before the LV turbine, separate components, MV PVC board and CPU chip line, HV gets an HV steam turbine. Hidden lines use FTB's per-quest flags on either side; crossings and long lines are notes in questgen check. D-277 Rocket Assembler (HV): 15 × 15 × 20 launch complex (twin stepped service towers, scaffold, umbilicals, crane bridge, flame trench), own casing with LDLib connected textures; the tier 1 rocket and its Ad Astra parts are made through GT and Ad Astra's own recipes for them are dropped. D-278 Mode-only quests: GTIACore tags the player gtia_journey or gtia_normal from the world preset (Custom counts as Normal); a hidden modes chapter turns the tag into an FTB Quests stage, and quests marked with a mode stay hidden in the other one. The Start chapter's strong tool rewards become the Journey Starting Kit; Normal gets steel tools and an LV prospector. D-279 Organ system ported from GTO 0.6 into GTIACore: 9 organ types × tiers 0–4, steel/fairy/mechanical wings, Organ Modifier screen (9 organ + 8 wing slots), organs kept in persisted player data. Effects as in GTO (leg speed scaled to +10/30/60/100 %, +5 armor and toughness per set tier, +4 reach, liver and lung perks, no hunger at set 3, flight at set 4). Ad Astra planets hurt players below set tier (t−1)/2+1 (Moon and Mars: 1). GTO assembler recipes; phantom membranes replace Botania in the cheap wings. GTO's "nano wall" is left out (GTOLib only). D-280 GTIA Rules grow from 44 to 52 for parity with GTO Rules: rubber tree chance, infinite bedrock fluids, require GT tools (restart), material hazards, extra regeneration (food threshold and strength), planets need organs, organ cost. GTO rules without a GTIA mechanic stay out (see the table below). D-281 MV/HV chemistry lines: Ostwald Converter (MV, cobalt oxide gauze; HV platinum gauze), Claus Unit, Kroll Reactor and Siemens Reactor (HV), Czochralski boule from 16 polysilicon in the EBF. Real stoichiometry and closed loops (NO, Mg/Cl₂, HCl). D-282 Main menu with FancyMenu 3.9.12 (Konkrete, Melody) instead of PackMenu: animated emblem plus the author's text logo recoloured in purple, animated pixel-art space-factory background, buttons Singleplayer, Multiplayer, Mods, Settings, Quit and Discord. D-283 Quest book highlight images: isometric renders of 19 multiblocks from the real textures (modpack/tools/iso_render.py). The Moon quest is a dimension task and the reachability model knows Ad Astra's own Moon blocks, so no lunar quest is pending.

docs.title: GTO Rules left out of GTIA Rules (D-280)
docs.text: GTO rule Why Recipe / mod recipe / ore processing difficulty, fluid resource difficulty, tech tree difficulty GTO-specific recipe sets; GTIA has one recipe set per pack, tuned by the recipe rules Scan duration, repeated scan factor, energy data hatch warm-up No research tree (D-226) Space elevator, ME hatch energy, ME simple pattern buffer, ME muffler amplifier, virtual coin Machines that only exist in GTO Generator array, wind turbine, magic generator, mega turbine, flow fuel cell, bio stimulation, wireless energy tower, lightning rod Generators that only exist in GTO Large steam circuit assembler, large solar boiler, large steam storage tank, dual chamber Steam machines that only exist in GTO; GTIA's steam rules cover the GTNA steam multiblocks Fluid pipe throughput, maintenance wear rate, random maintenance failures, configurable maintenance bounds, parallel hatch tier bonus, processing plant parallels, field generator amount, time twister, shut down on power loss, generators burn fuel when full, reset progress on low energy No setting in GTCEu 7.5.3 to drive them Tiered casings Kept off in both presets by an earlier pack decision Mob enhancement No mob changes in GTIA Circuit assembly line component amount No circuit assembly line in GTIA D-284 GTIA's own chemistry rules (54 rules in all): catalyst wear (Normal: 1 % chance per run that the Ostwald/Claus catalyst wears out; Journey: never) and heat recovery (Journey: 1.5× the steam of the chemistry plants). Organ textures redrawn; Organ Modifier screen shows the slots on a body outline with an effect readout. Main menu: one row of four textured buttons (Singleplayer, Multiplayer, Settings, Quit) and a Discord icon. D-285 The Android .mrpack ships from 0.1.0-dev-5: Modrinth links where the exact file exists, every CurseForge-only jar inside the pack with the author's permission (owners informed; removed at once on request). Built locally with tools/mrpack.py and attached to the release. D-286 Space age direction: the station lives in Ad Astra's orbit, starts in HV and is modular (a core plus connectors and modules that grow the station, with GTIA-only modules); the extreme-gravity destination is an Ad Astra planet (datapack). Three community stations (ABFielder "Space Station fiop", Toppat Orbital Station, Icarus), cleared for use by the author, replace Ad Astra's default station structures with GTNA ABS casings and Ad Astra plating, doors and lamps. Fouling and vein purity rules are approved. D-287 Quest book layout in the GTNH way: tools/quest_layout.py places Steam, LV, MV, HV, Agriculture and Bees in dependency columns ordered to minimise crossings, with leaf quests in a ring around the quest they hang from and large collections as a grid block; tier-wide hubs (7+ dependents) do not place quests and their lines are hidden; long lines, lines over a quest and lines crossing twice per line are hidden. Every dependency stays (reachability). Visible crossings: Steam 102 → 5, LV 78 → 4, MV 35 → 6, HV 31 → 4. Book theme: opaque dark background, thick red/green lines. Era banners as chapter images. D-288 Creating a world whose preset changes a startup rule asks for a restart first, like GTO's difficulty: "Save and Quit" writes the rules, closes the game and keeps the choice for the next create-world screen. Opening a saved world with other startup values asks too (Save and Quit / Play anyway). D-289 Agriculture (21 quests) and Bees (13 quests) chapters in the Systems group. New recipes for the empty Bee Cage, the Honey Treat (Mixer) and the Greenhouse controller, which had none; a GameTest now checks that every GTIA machine has a recipe. D-290 Mode quests are visible from the start in worlds of their mode: the Starting Kits complete with their Start step's task, and one opening quest per mode explains what it changes. D-291 The Start splits GTO-style into Welcome (reading, the world's mode, rules, community, EMI and Crafting Chain tips) and a step-by-step Start that snakes from the first log to the first Coke, with tips next to the steps that need them; the author's 29 quests keep ids, text, tasks and rewards. Steam supplies become per-mode kits. Tips in LV, MV and HV. Multiblock Goals chapter after GTNH's: all 254 multiblocks in a grid, columns by family, rows by the voltage their controller recipe needs, text from each mod's own tooltip. D-292 Multiblock renders leave the quest map and quest text (EMI's preview stays, press R); the era banner sits in the free space nearest the chapter's entry quest. D-293 Steam, LV, MV and HV take the GTNH 2.9 chapter structure: a quest with a GTNH equivalent goes to its place, GTIA-only quests sit next to the quest they depend on, no quests added; dependencies thinned by the reachability check to 1–2 per quest. Every chapter has its own low-contrast pixel-art background tile: Steam bronze, LV grey, MV blue, HV light steel, EV light purple, IV dark blue; Welcome dark brick, Start stone, Agriculture farmland, Bees honeycomb, Energy coils, Wireless circuit traces, reference chapters a neutral grid. D-294 Partly revised by D-345 (Pyrolyse Oven log recipes are back). No competing chemistry routes. 47 GTCEu/GTNA direct syntheses that skipped GTIA's chemistry lines are removed in both modes: aluminium (bauxite, sapphire, kyanite, clay and aluminium sulfite electrolysis; the bauxite sludge chain), sulfuric acid, ammonia, nitric acid, membrane-less chlor-alkali, soda ash, titanium tetrachloride and its reduction outside the Kroll Reactor, quicklime, chemical ethylene (cracking stays) and log pyrolysis. By-products (ores, distillation, recycling, silicate decomposition) stay. The GTCEu silicon boule stays because the HV Siemens Reactor needs HV circuits, which need wafers. Quests that relied on the old routes now point to GTIA's plants. D-295 Each Multiblock Goals quest gives a small pack of its row's metal (4 bronze, steel, aluminium, stainless steel, titanium or tungstensteel ingots; 2 of the LuV–UV metal; 1 neutronium), checked by the reachability tool. D-296 Steam, LV, MV and HV go back to the v7 layout (each quest's own x/y) until the new GTNH layout is approved: the D-293 layout hid the lines of 36–58% of the quests in each chapter and left 15–29 quests per chapter with no line at all. D-297 The GTNH layout is redone by the generator around GTNH's hubs: checked GTIA↔GTNH pairs; where a GTIA quest takes a GTNH hub, the quests under it depend on it (implied dependencies only); a GTNH hub with no GTIA pair becomes a GTIA milestone quest (imported or checkmark); the GTNH grid is compacted; GTIA-only quests branch in straight rows; quests move before lines are hidden; sizes 1/2/3. Targets: no quest without a line, at most 10% with hidden lines, no overlaps or lines over quests. D-298 Work moves to mechanics, processing lines and performance; the quest book comes last, before the public release. Changes target critical, specific points: GTCEu machines and multiblocks stay and get recipes with new materials, and a new machine is added only when no existing one can do the step. Alternative routes follow GTNH's model (for example three routes to aluminium ingots). D-299 Revoked by D-334. Nothing from GTNA or GTIA is removed (lines, recipe types, machines). Late GTNA machines are gated by their controller recipe: the Integrated Ore Processor around IV/LuV, the PCB Factory after LuV. D-300 Reusable machines and mechanics live in GTIACore (revises part of D-206). D-301 Multiblock structures are proposed by the assistant at the level of detail of GTNA's structures and approved by the author, starting with the Wood Retort, Lime Kiln and Diaphragm Cell. D-302 Superseded by D-335 (machines become recipes; structures archived). Chemistry slice 01 structures replace the D-251 boxes: Wood Retort as a brick bench with a wrought-iron retort, condenser and decanter (12×12×8); Lime Kiln as a banded shaft kiln with a hoist tower (7×14×5); Diaphragm Cell as a row of 3 to 9 Hooker cells, one parallel per cell, still limited by energy. D-303 The Integrated Ore Processor controller moves from the EV Assembler to the IV Assembly Line (7,680 EU/t). D-304 GTNH-style electrolyzer: 26 silicate and clay decompositions cost MV, 18 give Alumina instead of Aluminium (for the Hall-Héroult Cell), bastnasite gives Rare Earth instead of cerium; recycling and source ores stay. D-305 Dust-to-fluid extraction is removed for 13 EBF-only materials (Extractor and Liquefaction Furnace); parts and ingots still melt. Greenhouses, Tree Growth Simulator and Atomization stay as they are. D-306 Pig iron steelmaking with existing machines: PBF/EBF make Pig Iron and Slag from hematite or magnetite, coke and calcite; the LV Arc Furnace turns pig iron and oxygen into steel; slag replaces stone dust in concrete. D-307 Air separation stays as it is (LV Centrifuge, Vacuum Freezer, Distillation Tower). D-308 Three aluminium routes: dust in the EBF at HV (480 EU/t); dust pressed into Crude Aluminium and melted at MV, slowly; alumina and carbon in the EBF at MV, at half the Hall-Héroult yield. D-309 Naquadah reactor ladder in GTNA: the Large Naquadah Reactor (ported from GregTech Odyssey, UHV) and the Naquadah Hyper Reactor (GTNA original, UEV, four times the EU per mB, oxygen or nitrogen plasma boosters). GTNA adds Naquadah Fuel and Enriched Naquadah Fuel with simple default recipes; GT:IA will replace the fuel chain later. D-310 Veins with purity and the Entangled Miner: GTCEu bedrock ore veins return as a passive, infinite source from LV, each vein rolled impure ×1, normal ×2 or pure ×4. A Vein Card records a vein; the Entangled Miner (GTIACore single block, LV to IV) mines it remotely, 8 s per operation at 30 EU/t with normal overclocking (LV normal 900 raw ores per hour; IV pure 8 per second). At most 4 miners per vein; same dimension until HV, any dimension from EV. The GTCEu Bedrock Ore Miner is removed. Revises D-117. D-311 Frozen by D-333. First megastructure: the Matrioshka Brain, in GTIACore. Up to five computing shells around a star in its own dimension (the Nexus System, an Ad Astra planet; without Ad Astra the machine is absent), formed only there. Landauer physics: colder shells compute more, an overheated shell stops. Produces CWU (2^22 to 2^26 CWU/t) and a new resource, Ψ (thought cycles). Own 3D model, converted to a GTCEu pattern. D-312 Frozen by D-333. Eras beyond MAX, in GTIACore: voltage stops at MAX; each new tier is an era with its own condition, a non-EU resource and a megastructure that opens it, as a separate axis from voltage. Draft eras: Ψ (Matrioshka Brain), Stellar, Dimensional, Causal, Final, each with levels I to III. First delivery: the Matrioshka Brain and Era Ψ. How the game ends is up to the modpack. D-333 Restructuring. GTIA follows ten pillars (see Design pillars). Megastructures, the eras beyond MAX and the VFX engine are frozen: the code stays, no new work until HV has been played. Next playable target: Start → MV played and fixed, including MV AE2. D-334 Revokes D-299: GTIA and GTNA content can be cut or merged through the restructuring inventory. D-335 No custom chemistry multiblocks from Steam to HV. Wood Retort, Lime Kiln, Diaphragm Cell, Bayer, Hall-Héroult, Contact, Haber-Bosch, Solvay, Ostwald, Claus, Kroll and Siemens are removed; the real chemistry stays as recipes in GTCEu/GTNA machines (Coke Oven, Electrolyzer, Large Chemical Reactor, Autoclave, EBF). A new multiblock only when strongly needed (like GTO's Sintering Furnace). Approved structures are archived for IV+ Mega versions. The D-294 removals stay. The Rocket Assembler stays. D-336 Fermentation Vat (12 tiers), Catalytic Dehydrator and Still are removed; their recipes move to the GTCEu Fermenter, Chemical Reactor and Distillery. D-337 One Greenhouse: GTNA's (plus the Large Greenhouse), with Agronomica recipes. D-338 Survival stays out of the way: organs are an optional bonus with no Moon/Mars gate; vanilla hunger, no food mods; the End opens in EV with one recipe (no End Data per eye); GTNA Steam Elevator survival modules are conveniences only. D-339 Mining and building: a Fortune pickaxe in the starting kit, FTB Ultimine from the start, the personal dimension (ModernSpace) in Steam, the Entangled Miner stays in LV. D-340 AE2 storage and first automation in MV; HV refinement unlocks parts such as ExtendedAE's Assembler Matrix. Wireless energy: Flux Matrix with losses in HV, full wireless in EV. GTNA wireless steam only in Journey; Normal uses pipes. D-341 New EV power: fission reactor (GTNH/GTO port), nitrobenzene and high-octane fuels in the Large Combustion Engine, Large Gas Turbine on refinery gas. D-342 Space: Ad Astra planets up to EV with adjusted resources, GTIA's own planets from IV. One visit per destination, then everything by data (Void Miner, fluids). Zero gravity stays required in EV; a Cleanroom-like multiblock simulates it on the ground. D-343 Identity: eras named after the Kardashev scale; detailed GTNH-style multiblock tooltips plus one GTO-style joke line; nothing that skips a tier, shortcuts only as same-tier kits plus a GTNH-style vending machine; the GTIA Rules stay. D-344 Cleanup: old internal docs are deleted; GTNA is fully reorganised and optimised, trilingual comments that repeat the code are removed, and content GTIA does not use is hidden by pack config. D-345 The Pyrolyse Oven log recipes come back as the efficient MV wood route; the Coke Oven wood recipe stays the Steam one and replaces GTCEu's log to charcoal. D-346 Branches reach main only after the author tests the new chemistry in the client. D-347 The personal dimension portal is the reward of a Steam quest, with no crafting recipe. D-348 Starting mining kit: a Mining Hammer and a steel GregTech pickaxe with Fortune III, Unbreaking III and Efficiency III, in a Mining Kit quest for both modes. Fortune works on GregTech ores with the vanilla ore formula, the same in both modes. D-349 AE2 in MV, GTO-style: drives, controller, terminals and autocrafting in the MV Assembler with MV circuits, processors in the MV Laser Engraver. HV unlocks ExtendedAE's Assembler Matrix, crafting CPUs above 4k, extended pattern providers and interfaces, wireless terminals and P2P. D-350 Flux Matrix in HV: stainless steel and HV circuits, 3% loss in HV; no loss and cross-dimension network from EV. LV/MV wireless hatches stay but need the Flux Matrix. D-351 The Wireless chapter is redone with the quest atlas method after Start → MV. D-352 The Eye of Ender only comes from an HV Assembler recipe (HV emitters and sensors use it); the End opens in HV.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
Channel How it is made Who it is for Nightly Every push to main of the modpack replaces the nightly pre-release Testers who want the latest build dev / pre / alpha The Package workflow run by hand with a tag such as 0.1.0-dev-5, 0.1.0-pre-1 or 0.1.0-alpha Testers following a milestone beta The same workflow with a -beta tag The first channel published as stable

Only the newest release of each group is kept (the newest beta and the newest dev/pre/alpha); the nightly is never removed by a versioned release.

Changelogs and release notes are written in English. Mods (GTIACore, GTNA, Agronomica) release on their own and the pack pins exact versions with SHA-256 in manifest/full.lock.json.

docs.title: Mobile
docs.text: The pack targets Android through the Amethyst launcher with the .mrpack build, the same way GTNH supports mobile; the player guide is docs/MOBILE.md. The .mrpack is built by tools/mrpack.py (--test embeds the CurseForge-only mods, for private tests only). Only the official .mrpack with default configs is supported; mobile bugs use the mobile issue form.

docs.title: Design pillars
docs.text: GTIA is GregTech about building and running megafactories, on a Kardashev-scale arc: from the first steam machine to planetary, stellar and galactic engineering. It sits between GTNH, GregTech Odyssey and GregTech Leisure: GTNH's power options and detailed tooltips, GTO's fast early game and humour, GTL's clean pack without magic, and none of the free endgame items of GTL's modified editions.

docs.title: The ten pillars (D-333)
docs.text:
1. Kardashev scale. Eras are named after it; the endgame has Mega and Hyper blocks, Dyson spheres and Matrioshka brains.
  2. Survival is never a requirement. No dungeons, mob farming, food systems or exploration gates. Vanilla hunger.
  3. Mining without punishment. Good tools early, with Fortune that counts on GregTech ores; later the Entangled Miner.
  4. Easy building. FTB Ultimine from the start, the personal dimension in Steam, building gadgets and a multiblock builder.
  5. Early AE2. Storage and first automation in MV, refinement in HV.
  6. Space with purpose. Each destination has resources that make sense; visit once, then automate it by data.
  7. Many ways to make power, GTNH-style: steam turbines, combustion, semi-fluid, gas, then fission and nitrobenzene in EV.
  8. Wireless energy in HV–EV.
  9. Detailed multiblock tooltips like GTNH's, with a GTO-style joke line.
  10. Satisfactory feeling. Planning ratios and managing big factories, almost no survival.

docs.title: Working rules
docs.text:
• Grind is solved with more factory, never with more clicking.
  • Real chemistry, no PhD required, as recipes in GTCEu and GTNA machines. A custom multiblock is added only when no existing machine can do the job (D-335).
  • Nothing skips a tier. Shortcuts are same-tier kits and a vending machine, never free endgame items.
  • Every quest is reachable. A checker reads the pack's real recipes and fails the build if a quest asks for something you cannot make yet.

docs.title: What GTIA does not do
docs.text:
• No magic mods.
  • No research tree, research points or production quotas as gates.
  • No ULV era. The campaign goes Start → Steam → LV → MV → HV → …
  • Aesthetics never count toward progress.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
• Resource wells with purity, found by probe and worked by miners per tier.
  • Infinite sources per tier come from ordinary multiblocks (water pump, rock breaker…), never before Steam.
  • Renewables are real routes: agriculture → biomass → chemistry.
  • Mobs come only from the GTNA Industrial Slaughterhouse (LV), never from real mob farms.
  • Rare elements come only as by-products of specific lines.
  • Base chemicals have one real route each: GTIA's plants (Bayer and Hall-Héroult for aluminium, Contact, Haber, Ostwald, diaphragm chlor-alkali, Solvay and lime kiln, Kroll, wood retort and still, catalytic dehydration). GTCEu's direct shortcuts to the same products are removed; by-products of other lines stay (D-294).

docs.title: Farming
docs.text:
• Crops (Agronomica): crop sticks, stats and cross-breeding, inspired by GTNH's CropsNH and Forestry, with GTIA mechanics: NPK soil fed by the chemistry lines, climate controlled in the Greenhouse, pollination by bees, and phytomining (plants that recover metal from mining tailings).
  • Ore boost: 1 crushed ore + 1 leaf + a tier reagent → 3 purified ore, and the spent reagent goes back to be regenerated. The direct route (9 leaves → 1 dust) exists but is worse.
  • Bees (Productive Bees, from HV): base recipes removed; bees live as items inside the Industrial Apiary; combs only open in GregTech machines; new species from IV come from a mutation machine with a guaranteed result.
  • A crop or bee line yields per block about 10–25 % of the same tier's ore line. Its advantage is not needing a vein or a planet.

docs.title: Energy
docs.text:
• Every generator needs a real fuel line, with adjustable fuel blends.
  • Steam stays useful after the Steam age, and heat is a resource: exothermic reactions make steam.
  • Chemical and thermal storage, such as a molten-salt tank that stores heat and gives back steam.
  • Wireless energy has losses.

docs.title: Logistics
docs.text:
• No throughput limits as a mechanic. AE2 and wireless move things between areas.
  • No Create. Multiblock tanks and larger output hatches per tier.

docs.title: Danger
docs.text:
• Electrical explosions, hot and toxic fluids, radiation, with GTCEu's standard punishment.
  • Cleanrooms and inert atmospheres. Safety gear comes with corporate-humour quests.

docs.title: Modes (GTIA Rules)
docs.text: Journey, Normal and Custom presets, chosen when the world is created and then locked. Rules change recipes and numbers, never registries, so changing a preset never needs a game restart.

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text:
The full roadmap exists as a guide; a tier is only polished after the previous one has been played. Each chapter is drawn as a flowchart and approved before any quest is written.

Tier Line length Signature content Start — First tools, a Fortune pickaxe in the kit, FTB Ultimine Steam 2–3 steps Coke Oven wood and lime chemistry, fluxed steel, the GTNA large steam machines, personal dimension, first circuit by hand LV 4–6 Chlor-alkali in the Electrolyzer, real steelmaking, wood line to plastic, EBF and Aluminium, Entangled Miner MV 4–6 Gems and laser engraving, silicon and chips, stainless steel and Kanthal; Bayer, Hall-Héroult, Contact, Haber-Bosch and Solvay as recipes in GTCEu machines. AE2 storage and first automation. Agronomica crops in the GTNA Greenhouse HV 6–10 Full refining, AE2 refinement (Assembler Matrix), Flux Matrix wireless energy with losses, the Rocket Assembler and the Moon, bees EV 6–10 Full wireless energy, fission, nitrobenzene and gas turbines, Mars and Venus/Mercury, electric Void Miner per planet, zero gravity (in space or a ground simulator), the End IV+ 10+ GTIA's own planets, Mega versions of the chemistry plants (rotary kiln, membrane cell, Hall-Héroult lines, double absorption)

Gases come from planets: CO₂ on Mars, H₂SO₄ on Venus. Rare elements only appear as by-products of specific lines.

docs.title: Beyond MAX: eras
docs.text:
Voltage stops at MAX (D-312). Each tier after it is an era: a rule of its own, a resource that is not EU, and a megastructure that opens it. Eras are a separate axis from voltage, so GTCEu, GTNA and GTO keep their 15 tiers. Each era has levels I to III, unlocked by milestones of that era instead of bigger circuits. How the game ends is up to the modpack.

Era Opened by Resource New rule Ψ Matrioshka Brain (D-311) Ψ, thought cycles Computed recipes: items made from patterns by spending Ψ; Landauer's limit caps Ψ per second Stellar Stellar Engine Momentum The Nexus System travels the galaxy; each region has its own elements Dimensional Ringworld Curvature Machines run inside pocket dimensions opened by the Rift Gate Causal Birch World Causal debt Negative-duration recipes: output first, the bill later; too much debt causes a paradox Final Hyperquasaric megaconstruction Negentropy A finite world stock that every recipe of the era spends

The table is a draft. Megastructure work is frozen until HV has been played (D-333).
